deep.reconstruction:
PURPOSE. The heading reads 'Bestimmung der Elemente der Pallas aus den Oppositionen 2.3.4.5.' (Seeberg meridian; precession counted from 1803). Gauss starts from provisional Pallas elements: node Ω(1803) = 172°28'46.80", inclination i = 34°37'31.55", perihelion π(1803) = 121°5'9.84", eccentricity angle φ = 14°10'7.71" (e = sin φ). He then corrects π and φ by differential correction (x = dπ, y = dφ, both in arcseconds). The condition is that the mean anomalies at four oppositions (1804 Aug 30, 1805 Nov 29, 1807 May 4, 1808 Jul 26) imply one and the same mean motion. From that common motion he gets the mean motion, the semi-major axis and the epoch.

DATA (one row per opposition).
- t is days from 1803 Jan 0. Example: 365 + 243 = 608 for 1804 Aug 30. The values are 608.209491, 1064.471030, 1585.611736 and 2034.891076. The last is not 2034.821076; see corrections.
- The next column is the opposition (heliocentric) longitude l.
- Then the geocentric latitude b.
- Then log R, the Earth–Sun distance: 0.0038250, 9.9937332, 0.0039862, 0.0065917.
- 83.43" and 279.12" are the precession 50.1"/yr × t/365.25 to each date.
- The node of date is Ω + precession, e.g. 172°30'10.23". The same precession is added to π, so ω = π − Ω = 308°36'23.04" (mod 360) stays fixed.

CONSTANTS.
- log sec φ = 0.0134169.
- 3·log sec φ = 0.0402507, so log cos³φ = 9.9597493.
- log e = log sin φ = 9.3887752.
- log sin(φ/2) = 9.0910735.
- log(e·206264.8") = 4.7032003.

STEP 1 (reduction to the orbit; right-hand block, first four rows).
- l − Ω: 164°30'25.87", 254°49'30.09", 51°5'3.40", 131°29'33.78".
- Argument of latitude: tan u = tan(l−Ω)/cos i, with log cos i = 9.9153388. This gives u = 161°23'1.84", 257°25'6.73", 56°24'3.76", 126°2'55.07".
- The logs 9.4427768, 0.5666702, 0.0929374, 0.0533028 are log tan(l−Ω).
- The heliocentric latitude follows from tan β = tan i · sin(l−Ω), with log tan i = 9.8391694 and log sin(l−Ω) = 9.4267024, … .
- This gives β = 10°27'2.10", 33°40'50.67" (south), 28°14'51.28", 27°20'55.88". These are presumably for comparison with the latitudes; no comparison is written on the page.

STEP 2 (true anomaly). v = u − ω = 212°46'38.80", 308°48'43.69", 107°47'40.72", 177°26'32.03".

STEP 3 (eccentric anomaly), using the Theoria Motus form sin½(v−E) = sin½φ · sin v · sqrt(r/p), where p/r = 1 + e cos v.
- Rows: log|e cos v|; log(p/r); log sin v; ½log(p/r); log(sin v/√(p/r)); plus log sin ½φ.
- |v−E| = 8°35'36.59", 10°16'3.06", 14°1'30.09", 0°43'32.28". The sign is that of sin v.
- E = 221°22'15.39", 319°4'46.75", 93°46'10.63", 176°42'59.75".

STEP 4 (Kepler's equation).
- sin E is computed as cos φ · sin v/(1 + e cos v). The rows log(sin v/(1+e cos v)) and log sin E differ by 0.0134169.
- e·sin E in arcseconds: 33370.03", 33071.02", 50380.16", 2891.77".
- M = E − e sin E = 230°38'25.42", 328°15'57.77", 79°46'30.47", 175°54'47.98".

STEP 5 (partial derivatives).
- dM/dv = cos³φ/(1+e cos v)²: rows 9.9597493, 2·log(p/r), result.
- dM/dφ (v fixed) = −sin v · (2 + e cos v) · cos²φ/(1+e cos v)²: rows log(sin v/cos φ), log(2 + e cos v), and the sum with log dM/dv.
- Since dv = −dπ = −x: dM = −(dM/dv)x + (dM/dφ)y.
- Coefficients: −1.445093x + 1.447713y; −0.685132x + 1.185692y; −1.064839x − 2.013188y; −1.597061x − 0.129040y.

STEP 6 (mean motions over the three intervals).
- Δt = 456.261539, 521.14076 and 449.279344 days.
- ΔM = 351452.35", 401432.70", 346097.51".
- ΔM − 770·Δt = 130.965", 154.315", 152.415".
- The logs of these and of Δt (2.6592139, 2.7169550, 2.6525165) give n_k = 770 + (…)/Δt:
  - n₁ = 770.2870393 + 0.0016656x − 0.0005743y
  - n₂ = 770.2961100 − 0.0007286x − 0.0061382y
  - n₃ = 770.3392432 − 0.0011846x + 0.0041937y

STEP 7 (condition equations, ×1000).
- E1 = 1000(n₂ − n₁) = 9.0707 − 2.3942x − 5.5639y = 0.
- E2 = 1000(n₃ − n₂) = 43.1332 − 0.4560x + 10.3319y = 0.
- Elimination, all mine to verify:
  - A = 2E1 + E2 = 61.2746 − 5.2444x − 0.7959y.
  - B = E1 − 5E2 = −206.5953 − 0.1142x − 57.2234y.
  - C = −0.02174·A = −1.3321 + 0.1140x + 0.0173y.
  - D = −0.013889·B = +2.8694 + 0.0016x + 0.7948y.
  - B + C = −207.9274 − 0.0002x − 57.2061y.
  - A + D = 64.1440 − 5.2428x − 0.0011y.
  - This is a nearly diagonalising combination.
- Result: x = +12.24", y = −3.63". Hence π(1803) = 121°5'22.08" and φ = 14°10'4.08".

STEP 8 (mean motion and semi-major axis).
- Inserting x, y gives the sidereal (anomalistic) motion 770.30953"/day, log 2.8866652.
- Tropical motion = sidereal + 50.1"/365.25 = 770.44670"/day, log 2.8867426.
- Kepler III with Gauss's constant k = 3548.18761" (log 3.5500066): log(k/n) = 0.6633414, so log a = (2/3)·0.6633414 = 0.4422276 (a ≈ 2.768). Planetary mass is neglected.

STEP 9 (epoch; bottom block).
- Corrections to M at oppositions 2 and 5: −17.69 − 5.26 = −1.445093·12.24 + 1.447713·(−3.63); and −19.55 + 0.47 = −1.597061·12.24 − 0.129040·(−3.63).
- Corrected M: 230°38'2.47" and 175°54'28.90".
- Adding the corrected perihelion of date (121°6'45.51" = 121°5'22.08" + 83.43"; 121°10'1.20" = 121°5'22.08" + 279.12") gives mean longitudes 351°44'47.98" and 297°4'30.10".
- Reduced to whole days with the tropical motion: −0.209491 d → −2'41.40"; +0.108924 d → +1'23.92". This gives L(608) = 351°42'6.58" and L(2035) = 297°5'54.02".
- Check (mine): 1427 d × 770.4467" = 305°23'47.4" carries the first into the second.
- Back to t = 0: L(1803 Jan 0) = 221°34'54.97". This is the epoch on the next page (54.99").
errors: No substantive errors found; all checked arithmetic (angle subtractions, u, v, v−E, E, e·sinE, M, partial-derivative logs, interval differences, mean motions, condition equations, elimination, final x, y, a) reproduces to the last unit or nearly.
Minor slip: the interval 1585.611736 − 1064.471030 = 521.140706 is used as 521.14076 (5e-5 d). It only affects 154.315" vs 154.356" by 0.04", which is negligible.
Minor: the third interval is used as 449.279344 instead of 449.279340 (4e-6 d), negligible.
The y-difference −0.262023 vs the exact −0.262021 is a rounding difference only.
The node and perihelion are advanced by general precession in longitude only (50.1"/yr). This is a standard approximation, not an error at this level.
The heliocentric latitudes β are computed but no explicit comparison with the observed latitudes appears on the page.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine working sheet from Gauss's well-documented Pallas orbit computations (c. 1808–09). It applies the formulas of Theoria Motus (Gaussian conversion v→E, dM/dv, dM/dφ) to a differential correction of π and φ from four oppositions, followed by Kepler III with k. Nothing goes beyond his published methods. The only interest is as a dated numerical record (epoch 221°34'54.97", n = 770.4467", log a = 0.4422276). Also, the content (oppositions up to 1808) postdates the bundle label 1805.

transcription_corrections: Time of the 1808 Jul 26 opposition is 2034.891076, not 2034.821076. Confirmed by the interval 449.279344, the reduction +1'23.92" and the 1427-day check.
Third y-coefficient is −2.013188y, not +2.013188y. Its log 0.3038843 is positive, sin v > 0, and −2.013188 − 1.185692 = −3.198880.
Fourth y-coefficient is −0.129040y, not +0.129040y. Consistent with 1.884148 = −0.129040 + 2.013188 and with the +0.47 correction.
In the right column the y-coefficient of the second interval is −3.198880y; the arrow-like prefix is a minus sign.
'20580' and '24453' are the values 0.20580 and 0.24453 of |e cos v| (with interpolation notes 102/178 etc.).
'Comp. Cos. φ ... ‖ 3/4 ... 0,0402507' should read 3·comp.cos φ (= 3 × 0.0134169), i.e. log sec³φ.
Interval '521,14076' as written by Gauss (exact 521.140706); '449,2793440' as written (exact 449.279340).
Row labels at left: 'p/r' (log(1+e cos v)), 'sin' (log sin v), '√(p/r)', 'sin…/√' and, in the M block, 'sin v/(1+e cos v)' and 'sin E'.
